Printed candidate test statistics/p bounds (all from p. 376 Results): Retro-cue main effect on accuracy: higher with a retro-cue, all ps ⬍ .01.; Stimulus type × memory set size: significant, F(5, 55) ⫽ 11.51, p ⬍ .01, driven by ceiling perfor-; Retro-cue × memory load, all loads: memory load, F(5, 55) ⫽ 2.21, p ⬍ .07.; Retro-cue benefit at individual loads: mance at all memory loads ( ps ⬍ .05) except for Load 1 ( p ⬎ .70).; Retro-cue benefit at load two: two items in the memory array, p ⬍ .02 (Lepsien et al., 2005).; Retro-cue × memory load excluding load one: was not significant, F ⬍ 1.; Cue effect at set size one versus two: interaction was found, F(1, 11) ⫽ 4.80, p ⬍ .05, with an observed; Load two versus other loads: extreme value), no interaction was detected (Fs ⬍ 1).; Linear load × cue contrast: load and cue; that too was insignificant, F ⬍ 1.. F bounds retained as bounds; no metric conversion. p. 377 discussion and p. 380 Table A3 describe the same experiment but do not uniquely identify the requested test.
